To me, the version of Werewolf worth playing is One Night Ultimate Werewolf. To me, it takes everything wrong with werewolf, and makes it better.

  1. Werewolf has player elimination, One Night Ultimate Werewolf does not. Playing Werewolf is a drag when you're the first person killed and you spend the rest of the game waiting for it to end. This doesn't happen with One Night, because it happens in one Night.

  2. Scales Better with less players. Most games of Werewolf need at least 6 players (one of which is a moderator), while One Night can feasibly be played with as little as three. Yes the game is stronger with more players, but the fact that you don't need a five-man-pick up basketball team definitely helps.

  3. No moderator, this is a huge one for me because I would almost always be the moderator, thus I would never get to play.

  4. **Short games. ONUW takes less than 10 minutes to play, and everyone is involved with it the whole time. Traditional werewolf can take much longer. This means that ONUW allows you to play multiple games (and people will definitely want to.)

  5. (Almost) Everyone has an ability. Unless you play with some villagers, everyone has an ability, which brings their own knowledge to each round. While some versions of Werewolf do include this, it works great in ONUW because it doesn't turn into "Well, Sam is acting suspicious." It becomes a logic puzzle for the group to solve, except some of your clues might be outright lies. To me, having a game focus on game mechanics instead of people's abilities to lie make the game more interesting.

Going along with what Shagoosty said, I played a couple games of One Night Ultimate Werewolf this week. I've been wanting the game for a while now, and had the perfect excuse to get it with Halloween coming up, a trip up to see family, and needing something to post on this thread. :)

I've never played the game before, but my family are all big fans of The Resistance: Avalon, so I thought this couldn't miss. Boy, was I right.

Before I get to the gameplay, the components: I really liked that they went with thick cardboard for the roles, the only downside is the clacking around. Part of the game is swapping out cards while nobody is looking, but if you are loud you will give yourself away. Overall, great quality, really happy with everything in the box.

We played 6 games, the first being the typical rough start. You start the game with everyone getting a role, and after looking at your role, you close your eyes. I downloaded an app that announces when each role opens their eyes and performs an action, so we let that guide us, and it worked out well. The problem was the people following directions. I'm ashamed to say that I was one of the problems the first couple tries. I had the role of mason. There are two masons in the game, and their special ability is that they get to open their eyes and see each other. So, my role was called, I opened my eyes, and everyone else still had their heads down. I yelled out "HOLD IT". Told everyone that they need to pay attention to what the app is saying because there should have been another Mason. Well, there WAS another one, it just so happened that nobody was assigned that role. You see, there are three unclaimed roles that go in the middle of the table to keep people guessing on what is out there, and gives bluffers an advantage. So I was completely in the wrong there and had to hear about it for the next hour.

Once we got past the night time (heads down, eyes closed) phase, and all actions were preformed, WOW did we have fun. Everyone opened their eyes, and the accusations started flying. The best game we played had my father as the drunk. Now, the drunk (during the night phase when everyone's eyes are closed) has to take their card and exchange it with one of the middle cards WITHOUT looking at the card they receive. So basically, they are so drunk that they don't know who they are. We went around the room, and the robber explained who they were, and who's card they stole, the trouble maker explained who's card she swapped, etc... We had two werewolves in our group, and one claimed to be a villager, and the other claimed to be the seer. The seer gets to look at another person's card, or two of the middle cards. Well, that werewolf lucked out, because nobody else was claiming seer, so her story worked. And of course she claims she looked at the other werewolf's card and verified that she was a villager. So it all came back to the drunk. We had to kill him because we all thought that there HAD to be two werewolf cards in the middle and he must've grabbed one of them. We kill the drunk and wait for the reveal. Villager. Dang. Then it happened. The two werewolves revealed themselves, one of them being my 7 year old niece. We were all blown away. She had us SO CONVINCED that she was a villager, nobody saw that coming. Overall it was an unbelievably fun game, and I can't wait to get another session in.
